newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Holyman shares sink after U.K. warning.
newsitem.headline: Holyman shares sink after U.K. warning.

text.p: Shares in ferry operator Holyman Ltd sank over four percent to A$4.38 on Thursday in the wake of a warning on its U.K. operations.
Holyman said it had reduced 1997 expectations for its two thirds owned Holyman Sally operation after a review of its performance.
However, the company cautioned it was too early to be confident of any forecast results for the full year with the peak season yet to commence.

Holyman Sally operates high speed and conventional ferry services between Ramsgate, England and Ostende, Belgium, and between Ramsgate and Dunkirk, France. The Ramsgate-Ostende service commenced on March 1, and the Ramsgate-Dunkirk service on May 15 with Holyman saying the service was now fully operational for the peak season, commencing in July.
Brokers said the concerns over technical and operating difficulties expressed in the announcment were already in the market, with today's sharp fall in light trade a late reaction.
"That has been in the market for the last six months," said a senior dealer at a Sydney brokerage, noting Holyman's fall from its November 1996 record high A$6.00 to today's levels.
"It peaked at A$6.00, went close to A$4.00 and then bounced. This morning has just been the last wriggle," the broker said.
By 11.10 a.m. (0100 GMT), Holyman shares were 38 cents lower at A$4.19 on thin turnover of 33,287 shares.
